title: Personal Checking: Account-Count Ceilings for Each Customer
content:
## Clause

A customer may be primary owner of more than one Personal Checking account, but two ceilings bind at the same moment whenever a new account is to be opened:

1. **Product-wide ceiling.** Across all tiers, the customer's Personal Checking accounts that are not closed must number fewer than 4 when the new account is opened.
2. **Tier ceiling.** Among the customer's accounts of the tier being requested, those that are not closed must number fewer than that tier's own per-customer ceiling; every tier applies its own figure.

An account in applied, active, dormant, restricted or charged-off status is counted under both ceilings; only a closed account drops out of the count. Joint ownership is not recognised: an account is counted solely for the customer recorded on it as owner. If either ceiling has already been reached, the opening is refused and nothing is recorded.

## Evidence

Both counts are read from the bank's own account records for the customer (owner and status for the product-wide count; owner, tier and status for the tier count). What the customer says about the number of accounts held does not replace the records.

## Decision table

| Product-wide count below 4 | Tier count below the tier ceiling | Opening |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | may proceed |
| yes | no | refused, nothing recorded |
| no | yes | refused, nothing recorded |
| no | no | refused, nothing recorded |

## Hypothetical cases

- A customer holds three Personal Checking accounts: one active Everyday Checking, one dormant Interest Checking and one charged-off Access Checking. All three count, so the product-wide count is 3. Suppose, hypothetically, that the Access Checking ceiling were one account: a request for a second Access Checking account would then fail the tier count, because the charged-off Access Checking account still counts.
- The same customer's closed accounts, however many, add nothing to either count.
- A customer with four accounts that are not closed cannot open a fifth of any tier.
